buildflow.title: Turn on Firebase Storage
buildflow.detail: Needs the Blaze plan (a card), a budget alert, then Storage > Get started and deploy storage.rules. Until this is done every photo and file upload fails: posts, portfolio, job photos. Check that Google accepts your card; prepaid cards are sometimes refused. BuildFlow's own reminder is set for 31 Oct.

buildflow.title: Billing: not needed while founding contractors are free
buildflow.detail: Billing is a stub by design (src/lib/billing.ts, 'manual' mode); it is not broken and needs no database change. Revisit when the first founding trial nears its end: bank transfer or PayPal invoices first, then WiPay or PayPal subscriptions. Stripe is not available in Jamaica.

buildflow.title: Add real company details and get the legal pages reviewed
buildflow.detail: Production refuses to start until support email, company name, address, governing law and NEXT_PUBLIC_LEGAL_REVIEWED=true are set. The Privacy Policy and Terms still contain placeholders. I can draft wording; a lawyer must review it.

buildflow.title: Move BuildFlow's Vercel project to Pro before charging
buildflow.detail: Hobby is non-commercial. Set the production environment variables at the same time (Firebase values, service account key as a secret, legal and support variables).
buildflow.src: Integration test report, P2-5; Firebase checklist

buildflow.title: Choose the production Firebase project and deploy it properly
buildflow.detail: Decide build-6fa95 or buildflow-prod. Enable Email/Password, add the Vercel domain to authorised domains, set the email sender name, deploy rules, indexes and storage, turn on daily backups. Seed reference data on any new project before anyone signs up.

buildflow.title: Add push notifications for new leads
buildflow.detail: Without them a contractor never hears about a lead unless the app is open, the main reason a tester would stop using it. You register the Android app in Firebase; I add google-services.json and the push plugin.

buildflow.title: Run the Android app on a real phone
buildflow.detail: Check the photo picker, PDFs, back button, offline launch and Android 15 layout. The app has never run on a device.

buildflow.title: Create the Android upload keystore and back it up
buildflow.detail: Keep it outside git. Losing it means you cannot update the app. Set CAP_SERVER_URL to the production address.

buildflow.title: Prepare the Google Play listing
buildflow.detail: 512px icon, 1024x500 feature graphic, at least 2 phone screenshots, short and full descriptions, category, content rating, Data safety form, reviewer test account. I can draft the texts. Check Play Console for the current closed-testing tester requirement for new accounts.

buildflow.title: Sign 10 founding contractors (your strongest skill)
buildflow.detail: Free for 60 days in exchange for feedback, a set of job photos and a testimonial. Pitch: your leads are yours, one flat monthly price, WhatsApp-first. Share each contractor's profile link or QR with their own customers, since a directory has no value without both sides.

buildflow.title: Test the price with real contractors
buildflow.detail: $50/month including 1 user, +$20 per extra user, is a bet and has not been validated. Ask each founding contractor: would you pay this, in USD or JMD, and is a cheaper solo tier needed?

buildflow.title: Study ClickAway, the Jamaican competitor
buildflow.detail: A local matching app with job bidding and payments, reported at about 2,800 beta users. BuildFlow's angle: leads are yours, flat price, built for the field.

buildflow.title: Decide on messaging
buildflow.detail: Private client link or in-app chat. Today customers contact contractors by quote request, phone or WhatsApp.

buildflow.title: Hardening: error monitoring, photo thumbnails, Content-Security-Policy
buildflow.detail: Agent work once the P0 items are clear: Sentry-style monitoring, thumbnails once Storage is on, and a CSP header.
buildflow.src: Integration test report, P2-2 to P2-4

system.title: Connect Twilio WhatsApp alerts
system.detail: Create the account, join the sandbox, add TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM and WHATSAPP_TO in Vercel.

system.title: Add the Anthropic key and token prices
system.detail: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (Secret) plus LLM_PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK and LLM_PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK from the pricing page. The $80 cap is already set.

system.title: Upgrade this project's Vercel team to Pro before real revenue
system.detail: Hobby is non-commercial. Also unlocks longer functions and more frequent cron.

system.title: Turn off Vercel Deployment Protection for production
system.detail: Needed so the phone app can load the manifest. The owner login protects the data.

system.title: Create a Solana address only if you go after Superteam bounties
system.detail: They pay in USDC/USDG on Solana; Treasury watches EVM chains only.

sources_setup.title: Add a GitHub token (read-only, no scopes)
sources_setup.detail: Raises Scout's GitHub search rate limit so it can look further before giving up. Create one at GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens (classic, no scopes needed, read-only is fine). Add GITHUB_TOKEN as a Secret in Vercel.

sources_setup.title: Create an Upwork profile
sources_setup.detail: The largest general freelance market; $500+ fixed-price web/app work is common. Its job feed closed its public API in 2024, so this needs a manual profile and proposals - I can draft proposal text once you're set up.

sources_setup.title: Create a Contra profile
sources_setup.detail: No-fee, portfolio-first marketplace. A good fit for showing your BuildFlow and funnel work directly.

sources_setup.title: Apply to Braintrust
sources_setup.detail: Vetted talent network; the client pays the platform fee, so you keep more of the rate.

sources_setup.title: Apply as a Webflow/Framer Expert or Partner
sources_setup.detail: Matches your website/funnel-building skill directly; these directories route client work to listed experts.

sources_setup.title: Optional: create a Freelancer.com account
sources_setup.detail: Scout already reads Freelancer.com's public listings with no login. An account is only needed to actually bid - not required for discovery.

sources_setup.title: Optional: apply to Toptal, Gun.io or Arc.dev
sources_setup.detail: Vetted developer networks with larger projects; screening is extensive, worth it only once you want bigger, steadier work.

items.title: Turn on Firebase Storage for BuildFlow
items.detail: Blaze plan + budget alert, then Storage > Get started, deploy storage.rules. Unblocks every photo/file upload. 20 min.

items.title: Decide BuildFlow's first billing method
items.detail: Bank transfer or PayPal invoice for your first 10 contractors, while WiPay/PayPal integration gets built. One decision, not a build.

items.title: Run Scout + review the board
items.detail: Click Run Scout now. Approve anything genuinely $500+ or easy; note which human-only Superteam listings you'll do yourself this week.

items.title: Study: registering YardScale Digital in Jamaica
items.detail: Companies Office of Jamaica (ORC) business registration steps, cost, timeline. 30 min research, write down what you need.

items.title: Draft BuildFlow's company details for the legal pages
items.detail: Real support email, company name (YardScale Digital or BuildFlow entity), address, governing law. I'll draft the Privacy Policy/Terms text; a lawyer still needs to review before launch.

items.title: Work one human-only Superteam listing yourself
items.detail: Pick the best-scoring one that's still open. Real work, real submission, tracked as a job in the system once submitted.

items.title: Study: Jamaica crypto off-ramp routes
items.detail: Test a small Binance->bank or Wise conversion if you're comfortable, so the route is proven before a real payment needs it.

items.title: Weekly loop: review what Scout found this week so far
items.detail: One line per rejected opportunity: why, and whether a scoring rule should change. This is the Monday loop from docs/runbooks/IMPROVEMENT_LOOP.md, run a day early this week.

items.title: Confirm BuildFlow's production Firebase project
items.detail: build-6fa95 or a fresh buildflow-prod - pick one, I'll update .firebaserc and the deploy checklist.

items.title: Run Scout + Operator; approve/reject the queue
items.detail: Keep the decision queue at zero. Every approval or rejection also trains the scoring via the weekly review.

items.title: Study: what contractors actually pay for
items.detail: Read 3-5 reviews/complaints of Jobber, Housecall Pro or similar on G2/Capterra. Real pain points sharpen BuildFlow's pitch and the missed-call offer.

items.title: List 3-5 contractors you could approach as founding users
items.detail: Doesn't need to be 15 - even 3 real names is enough to start. Past Needham's Construction / Yardscale contacts count.

items.title: Run Scout + Operator
items.detail: Standard daily pass.

items.title: Study: one Freelancer.com or Upwork proposal that won
items.detail: Find one publicly-discussed winning proposal in your field, note its structure. Feeds the proposal-writer skill later.

items.title: Pitch BuildFlow to at least 1 of the contractors from Thursday
items.detail: Free for 60 days in exchange for feedback, photos, a testimonial. First real signal on the $50 price.

items.title: Run Scout + Operator
items.detail: Standard daily pass.

items.title: One platform improvement
items.detail: Pick one real friction point from this week (a scoring miss, a confusing page, a missing field) and fix just that one thing.

items.title: Verify Storage actually works end to end
items.detail: BuildFlow's own reminder is set for today. Upload a logo and a job photo on the live site; confirm no 'Upload failed' error.

items.title: Light day: read, don't build
items.detail: Skim the week's Founder's Log entry, Scout's run history, and the daily reports. Notice patterns, don't act on everything.

items.title: Weekly review: revenue, pipeline, what changed
items.detail: Verified revenue, opportunities qualified vs rejected, BuildFlow blockers cleared. Write one line in the Founder's Log.

items.title: Set next week's 3 priorities
items.detail: Not a full re-plan - just the top 3 things that matter most going into next week.

acquire.goal: First 5 founding contractors using BuildFlow, free for 60 days in exchange for feedback, job photos and a testimonial (decided 29 Oct: free, not $10). Payment is a later step, so the success metric is five active contractors, not revenue. The engine is 2 faceless short videos a day that give value for a comment and ask for a short setup call.
acquire.thesis: Every video does one job: trade something genuinely useful for a comment or DM, then move the person to a 15-minute setup call. No face, no phone camera: everything is built on a computer from screen recordings, text, stock or AI footage and a voiceover (or captions only).
beats: One line of on-screen text naming a contractor pain in their words, e.g. "You quoted 3 jobs this week. How many did you follow up?"
Show the mess: a WhatsApp thread, a notebook, a lost invoice. Screenshot or stock b-roll.
Show the fix: a screen recording of BuildFlow doing that exact task (quote, client list, job photos, profile link).
Name the giveaway: "I made a free quote follow-up script pack." Show it on screen.
"Comment QUOTE and I'll send it." Keyword comment is the interaction that feeds the algorithm.
End on the first frame's text so it replays, which lifts watch time.
formats: BuildFlow on a laptop/emulator doing one job in under 15s. Fully camera-free. The proof format.
Kinetic text over stock footage: "3 mistakes that cost contractors jobs". Quick to batch.
Left: paper and WhatsApp chaos. Right: the same job in BuildFlow.
Scroll through a free quote/invoice/checklist and offer it for a comment.
One stat or rule of thumb (how to price a job, deposit norms) as an animated slide. Mark any figure you cannot source as an estimate.
Text-message style conversation: a customer asks for a quote at 9pm, contractor answers late. Two chat bubbles, no actor.
offers: WhatsApp message templates for quote follow-up, deposit and review requests. Cheapest to make, fits WhatsApp-first trade.
Simple PDF or sheet in JMD and USD.
What to photograph before, during and after a job.
The call itself is the offer: "I'll set up your public profile and first quote with you in 15 minutes."
"How to check a contractor before you pay" checklist. Drives consumers to profiles.
funnel: Watch the 3-second hold and completion rate per format
Target and track per format; this is the real signal
DM with the giveaway plus one question about their trade
Capture trade, parish, how they quote today
Offer two time slots; use a booking link
Profile live and first quote or job photo added
Counts toward the 5. Payment comes later
acquire.experiment: Run 10 days, 20 videos. Rotate the 6 formats evenly so each gets about 3 posts, hold the offer and CTA constant per 5-video block, and log views, comments, DMs and calls per video in one sheet. After day 10 keep the top 2 formats and drop the rest. Everything below is a planning assumption until the log says otherwise: expect most videos to do little, so judge on comments per 1,000 views and calls per 10 DMs, not on any single hit.
risks: Free users still need a working app: Firebase Storage must be on before any setup call or photos fail. Billing does not block this.
BuildFlow is not launch-ready (Storage, billing, legal are open). A call that ends in a broken upload loses the user. Fix Storage and decide billing first, or sell as a guided beta.
Collecting names and numbers in DMs: have a one-line consent note and the legal pages in place.
Platform rules on giveaways, automated DMs and AI footage differ; check each platform's current rules before using auto-reply tools.
No view or conversion figures are known yet. Nothing here is a forecast.
open: Which trade first (roofers, electricians, plumbers, general builders)? One trade makes the hooks sharper.
Voiceover (your voice, no face) or captions only?
Consumer-side giveaway: e.g. a free checklist for hiring a contractor safely. Worth doing once 2-3 contractor profiles are live.

tasks.detail: The only blocker for free founding users. Billing is not needed yet.

tasks.title: Build the first free giveaway
tasks.detail: Quote follow-up WhatsApp script pack as a PDF in JMD/USD context. Agent drafts, you review.

tasks.title: Write 20 storyboards from the 6-beat template
tasks.detail: Scene by scene: on-screen text, visual source, voiceover line, CTA keyword. Rotated across the 6 formats for the 10-day test.

tasks.title: Pick the no-camera toolchain
tasks.detail: Tab S9 FE: built-in screen recorder for demos plus CapCut or Descript for editing. Stock footage and captions or voiceover. No camera needed.

tasks.title: Set up a 15-minute booking link and a keyword-to-DM flow
tasks.detail: Booking page with a buffer, and a saved DM reply that sends the giveaway and the link.

tasks.title: Create the per-video log
tasks.detail: One row per video: format, hook, views, comments, DMs, calls booked, set-ups, paid. Can live in the dashboard later.

tasks.title: Post 2 a day for 10 days, then review
tasks.detail: Keep the top 2 formats, cut the rest, write what changed in the Founders Log.

tasks.title: Make the founding trial 60 days
tasks.detail: BuildFlow currently creates a 14-day trial for every business (onboarding.ts). For founding contractors it needs 60, as a code change in the BuildFlow repo.

tasks.title: Pick the first trade to target
tasks.detail: One trade for the first 10 days so the hooks and DM script stay specific.

decisions: Free for founding contractors (60 days), in return for feedback, job photos and a testimonial.
TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, Instagram. One edit exported to all four.

Two sides: contractors and construction service professionals (the buyers), and consumers who want trustworthy people to hire (the demand that makes the profile worth having). Contractor-first: consumer videos point to contractors' public profiles, and each founding contractor shares their own link.
Samsung Tab S9 FE only. Faceless formats need no camera: use the built-in screen recorder for demos, and stock or AI footage, text and captions for the rest, so camera quality does not matter.
